messages:
maya: seeing p99 jump on ingestion hosts, KV prefix hit-rate plummeted from ~78% to 9% at 09:03 UTC :eyes:
liam: looking, saw a routing change deployment at 08:58 that repointed some tenants to a shadow pool
sophia: stacktrace or metrics?
maya: posting dashboard snippets and kv stats
maya: ```
metric: prefix_hit_rate host=ingest-4 avg=0.092 timestamp=1719999990
kv.evictions/sec=12.4
request_latency.p99=420ms
```
andrew: perf-bot flagged kernel selection fallback on those nodes around 09:00
perf-bot: Alert: kernel_fallback=quant_kernel->int8_generic at 1719999986 reason="unsupported opset for optimized kernel"
liam: that kernel fallback increases per-token compute 2.3x, would amplify hot-tenant effects
devon: also noticed a surge in unique prefix cardinality from one tenant (tenant_id=acme-x) — prefixes with millisecond timestamps
sophia: can we see sample keys?
maya: ```
sample prefixes (count=5):
"user:acme-x:ts:1700000000001"
"user:acme-x:ts:1700000000123"
"user:acme-x:ts:1700000000456"
```
liam: yep that's basically cache poison — prefix granularity changed, cache keys exploded
andrew: rollout at 08:58 was a client change that increased prefix entropy by design for ordering
devon: quick mitigation: change routing to bypass shared prefix cache for that tenant, or apply prefix normalization policy
maya: tried a soft-route to dedicated bucket, hit-rate recovered to 65% in 4m and p99 dropped to 110ms
sophia: nice, can we make a durable mitigation? we should auto-detect sudden prefix entropy increases and either 1) enforce normalization, 2) isolate tenant, or 3) fallback to larger batch sizes
liam: note: kernel selection bump made the recovery slower; even after isolating, int8_generic is slower for long-seq so we still have residual latency
andrew: propose short-term: auto-isolate on prefix-cardinality delta > 10x within 5m and roll back the kernel fallback where safe
devon: I'll open a PR to add prefix-cardinality alert and a routing runbook
maya: thanks — created an incident doc and pinned quick commands in the channel
maya: ```
# quick commands
./infra_tool route set --tenant acme-x --bucket dedicated-temp
kubectl rollout undo deploy/client-service -n prod --to-revision=rev-2026-03-18
```
sophia: we should also add a kernel-selection guard: don't fallback to generic kernels for nodes serving high KV hit caches
liam: agenda for postmortem: 1) why client change wasn't flagged, 2) kernel fallback interaction, 3) automated isolation
maya: assigning actions: @devon alert+PR, @andrew kernel-fallback rollback policy, @liam postmortem writeup
perf-bot: Incident status=mitigated at 1720000419
maya: closing thread, will link postmortem once PR merged :white_check_mark:
